dossier.public_summary: The dip varies strongly from transit to transit and shows a second eclipse about a third as deep as the main one, which is expected for two stars eclipsing each other. The star also varies by tens of thousands of ppm at a period near the dip period, and the dip depth changes by four standard deviations - all best explained by an eclipsing binary or blended binary, not a 2.7-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depths are not consistent: sector 21 depth 933 ppm err 304 ppm vs sector75 depth 1087 ppm err 121 ppm combine to variable signal; transit depth scatter is highly significant for 3 transits, as in false alarm/some EB scenarios, not a repeatable planet.
Strong secondary ~38% of primary depth well above noise indicates stellar companion, not a hot-Jupiter occultation; detected per tool not a background artifact.

Large out-of-eclipse swing at the 14.7 d period and star is VARIABLE with spot amplitude 10532 ppm favours spotted/EB variability tied to period; duration ratio 1.11 and flat bottom favour EB over grazing planet.
